How does the standing up and typing feel?

It's different. I'm used to my elbows being lower than the keyboard, usually resting on the arm rest of the chair. Now they're level with or slightly above the keyboard, and I'm actively holding my arms up.

I also find myself looking at the keyboard more to find the keys. I'm ~80 WPM hunt-and-peck typing, but with my wrists and elbows oriented differently my typing is off just a bit. It shouldn't be too difficult to adjust to, just might take a few days.

I had an electric sit-to-stand for years. However, without one of those foam pads or some pretty heavy duty footwear, the pain never "passed." Instead, my feet got so sore that it started impacting my exercise regimen, so I cut out all the standing (I don't really want to cruise around the office in boots that would give my feet and ankles the support they'd need to be on them for that long without pain). For me typing wasn't bad because I could bring the desk to well above my waist level and type with my arms in a natural postion.

Some people swear by them, so when people ask me what they think I always say give it a try, but I've found sitting in a regular chair where I force myself to have proper posture has been the best for my neck. My back really has rarely bothered me - sometimes a bit in the summer if I ride my motorcycle a whole bunch, it's a gixxer and I'm 6'1" - but my neck kills after losing a disc up there. Just sitting up straight has been the best for that.

We also have some treadmill desks at work. That seems nice if you want to get some really light exercise in while working, but I'm not sure how tremendously beneficial it would be if you've got a moderate+ level of cardio conditioning.
